text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where code changes are automatically built and tested many times a day. Instead of waiting until a project is finished, developers regularly merge their work into a shared repository. Each merge triggers a CI pipeline, which first compiles the code into a working build. Once the build is successful, the pipeline runs a suite of automated tests. This process is essential because it catches issues early, before they become major problems. For example, a small coding error can be detected immediately, allowing the team to fix it while fresh in their minds. By making these checks routine, CI keeps the software stable and reduces the stress of debugging later.
